title: The word "meme" is coined
description: Richard Dawkins's book The Selfish Gene introduced "meme" as a unit of cultural evolution, an idea that copies itself from mind to mind the way a gene copies itself from body to body. He was not thinking of cats.

title: Godwin's law
description: Attorney Mike Godwin observed that as a Usenet discussion grows longer, the probability of a comparison to Nazis or Hitler approaches one. He meant it as an experiment in memetics, to push back on comparisons that trivialize the Holocaust. It made the Oxford English Dictionary in 2012.

title: The Dancing Baby
description: A 3D baby doing the cha-cha, made as a demo for the animation software Character Studio, became one of the first viral videos. It went from email forwards to Ally McBeal.

title: The Hampster Dance page goes up
description: Art student Deidre LaCarte made a GeoCities page of dancing hamster GIFs, set to a sped-up loop of Roger Miller's "Whistle-Stop" from Disney's Robin Hood, to win a web traffic contest with her sister and best friend. It got about four visits a day for a year and a half, then spread by email in 1999 and became one of the earliest internet memes.

title: "All your base are belong to us" video posted
phrase: the "All your base are belong to us" video
description: The European Mega Drive release of Toaplan's shooter Zero Wing opened with a famously garbled translation. A techno remix of the cutscene with an animated music video, posted to Newgrounds, sent the line everywhere. The Japanese original says, more or less, "All of your bases have been taken over by CATS."

title: The Star Wars Kid video goes online
description: Ghyslain Raza, 14, filmed himself swinging a golf ball retriever like Darth Maul's lightsaber and left the tape at school. He never meant anyone to see it, but a schoolmate found the tape and it went online. The ridicule was cruel enough that he left school for private tutoring. He has since spoken out about cyberbullying.

title: Numa Numa Dance uploaded
description: Gary Brolsma lip-synced, with feeling, to O-Zone's "Dragostea din tei" from his desk chair and posted it to Newgrounds. "Numa numa" comes from the Romanian "nu mă, nu mă" in the chorus.

title: Leeroy Jenkins video posted
description: A World of Warcraft guild carefully works out a plan for Upper Blackrock Spire while Leeroy is away making chicken. He comes back, shouts his own name, and charges in. Everyone dies. Blizzard later added him to the game.

title: I Can Has Cheezburger? starts
phrase: the first lolcat on I Can Has Cheezburger
description: Eric Nakagawa posted a picture of a hopeful cat captioned "I can has cheezburger?" and kept going. The blog brought lolcats and lolspeak into the mainstream and sold for $2 million eight months later.

title: Chocolate Rain uploaded
description: Tay Zonday's deep-voiced song, with a caption explaining "I move away from the mic to breathe in," became the viral video of summer 2007. The jokes mostly skipped what the lyrics are about: racism against African Americans.

title: The first Rickroll
description: A 4chan user linked to "Never Gonna Give You Up" in place of a Grand Theft Auto IV trailer. It grew out of "duckrolling," which did the same with a picture of a duck on wheels.

title: Charlie Bit My Finger uploaded
phrase: the upload of "Charlie Bit My Finger"
description: A father in England posted 56 seconds of his sons Harry and Charlie so their grandfather in the US could see it. Charlie bites, Harry is betrayed, and it was the most-viewed video on YouTube from 2009 to 2012.

title: YouTube Rickrolls its front page
description: For April Fools' Day every featured video on YouTube's home page led to "Never Gonna Give You Up," taking the Rickroll mainstream.

title: Trollface drawn
description: Carlos Ramirez, an 18-year-old college student in Oakland, drew it in Microsoft Paint for a comic about how pointless trolling is. Trolls adopted it anyway. He registered the copyright and has earned more than $100,000 from it.

title: David After Dentist uploaded
description: Seven-year-old David DeVore Jr., still woozy from anesthesia, asks his dad, "Is this real life?" His father meant to share it with family and missed the private option.

title: The Doge photo of Kabosu
description: Kindergarten teacher Atsuko Sato posted a picture of her rescued Shiba Inu, Kabosu, to her blog. Add some Comic Sans and it became Doge: such meme, very 2013, wow.

title: Nyan Cat
description: Christopher Torres drew a cat with a Pop-Tart for a body during a Red Cross donation livestream, after viewers suggested both. Set to a Japanese Vocaloid song and left to fly through space trailing a rainbow, it was one of the most-watched YouTube videos of 2011.

title: Grumpy Cat on Reddit
description: Tardar Sauce's frown came from an underbite and feline dwarfism. Her owners said that "ninety-nine percent of the time she is just a regular cat."

title: "This is fine"
description: KC Green's Gunshow strip "On Fire" has a dog sipping tea in a burning room. The meme is the first two panels. In the other four the dog melts.

title: Dogecoin launched
description: Software engineers Billy Markus and Jackson Palmer made a cryptocurrency with Kabosu's face on it as a joke about crypto speculation. In 2021 its market value peaked above $85 billion.

title: The Ice Bucket Challenge
description: Co-founded by Pat Quinn and Pete Frates, a baseball player diagnosed with ALS in 2012, it had people dumping ice water on their heads and calling out friends to do the same. It raised over $115 million for ALS research in 2014.

title: The dress
description: A photo of a dress for a wedding on the Scottish island of Colonsay went viral on Tumblr. Was it blue and black or white and gold? It was blue and black, and vision scientists studied why so many saw it otherwise.

title: Grumpy Cat dies
description: Tardar Sauce, the internet's grumpiest cat, died at seven.

title: Kabosu, the Doge dog, dies
description: The Shiba Inu behind Doge and Dogecoin died at 18. In Japan she was known less as a meme than as the star of one of the country's most popular pet blogs.
